2. Number of elements in each row
3. Type or number of elements printed in each row
For a pattern containing dollars and stars, these entities determine the number of loops required.
Therefore, three loops can be used to represent these three entities.
2. How can a pattern with three rows, five dollars, and five stars be implemented using nested loops?
The outer loop controls the number of rows.
The third loop prints five stars.

9. How can a pattern be divided into two separate patterns?
Some complex patterns can be treated as two independent patterns.
Each half can be implemented separately and then combined.
The first half can use one set of loops, while the second half can use another set.
If the second half is the reverse of the first half, the first loop structure can be copied and modified by reversing the required loop direction.
This approach simplifies complex pattern programs.

Similarly, changing the ending condition can remove a particular last row.
The starting and ending values of loops directly control which rows are produced.
